schema.label: Step 0
schema.text: Register, then obtain a standard-of-care PET/CT or PET/MR (PET1) with any FDA-approved prostate radiotracer before treatment planning. PET1 may be done during Step 0 or up to 16 weeks before Step 0. Record prostate fossa, intra-pelvic, and extra-pelvic sites. Extra-pelvic means any bone metastasis, or soft tissue, node, or organ disease above the common iliac bifurcation or outside standard prostate bed plus whole-pelvis fields. Step 1 randomization must occur within 7 days of Step 0 registration.

schema.label: Step 1, after Amendment 11
schema.text: The schema figure for patients enrolled after Amendment 11 shows only PET-positive extra-pelvic disease. Stratify lymph node sites only versus any non-lymph node site. Every patient on Arms C and D receives standard salvage therapy: prostate bed and pelvic lymph node external-beam RT plus a protocol-listed GnRH agonist or antagonist for 6 months. ADT may start from 7 days before Step 0 through 14 days after Step 1. RT starts after Step 1, from 7 days before ADT through 3 months after ADT starts. Apalutamide 240 mg by mouth once daily starts after Step 1 and within 28 days of ADT, and continues for 6 months. No randomization ratio is printed. The prostate bed and pelvic dose is institutional standard of care, not a fixed protocol dose.

arms.label: Arm C
arms.text: Standard salvage RT, 6 months of ADT, and apalutamide, with no upfront metastasis-directed RT. Metastasis-directed RT is allowed later for radiographic progression by PET or conventional imaging, or for persistent extra-pelvic PET disease after protocol treatment.

arms.label: Arm D
arms.text: Standard salvage RT, 6 months of ADT, and apalutamide, plus upfront metastasis-directed RT to all technically feasible PET-positive metastases during the 6 months of ADT. Options are SBRT 30 Gy in 3 fractions, with at least 40 hours between treatments for an individual field, reducible to as low as 35 Gy in 5 fractions, or non-SBRT 50 Gy in 10 fractions. Non-SBRT dose reductions are also permitted to meet constraints.

schema.label: PET2
schema.text: On Arms C and D, if PET1 used Axumin or flotufolastat F 18 (Posluma), repeat that tracer at PSA recurrence, at a clinical indication, or at 12 months after systemic therapy, whichever comes first. Other PET1 tracers do not receive a protocol PET2.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival from randomization: radiographic progression by conventional imaging or standard PET, cancer-related symptoms, or death.

eligibility: Step 0: Male and age 18 or older, with histopathologically proven prostatic adenocarcinoma treated by radical prostatectomy, ECOG performance status 0-2, and a candidate for standard post-prostatectomy RT to the prostate bed and pelvic nodes with ADT.

Biochemical recurrence meets one of three rules: PSA at least 0.2 ng/mL if the first detectable PSA was within 12 months after prostatectomy, and a persistent post-prostatectomy PSA of at least 0.2 ng/mL is eligible; PSA at least 0.5 ng/mL if the first detectable PSA was more than 12 months after prostatectomy; or any detectable PSA if baseline standard PET shows at least one positive lesion.

From Addendum 11, conventional imaging within 26 weeks before Step 0 must show no definite extra-pelvic metastatic disease. If there is no prior conventional imaging, it is optional when PET is positive for extra-pelvic lesions and is not required when PET is negative for extra-pelvic lesions. Non-osseous pelvic lesions are allowed if they fit in standard salvage fields.
Short-term ADT must not start before baseline PET. It may start after PET and up to 7 days before registration. A short course of low-dose antiandrogen, generally after PET1, is allowed as a bridge.

The patient must not be on another therapeutic trial, must tolerate lying flat for PET and radiation planning, and a PET/MR must meet local MRI safety rules. No seizures, and no stroke or head trauma with loss of consciousness, within 1 year. No inflammatory bowel disease or absorption disorder expected to make pelvic RT risk unacceptable by institutional standard.

Labs within 8 weeks before Step 0: hemoglobin at least 9.0 g/dL, independent of transfusion or growth factors within 3 months; leukocytes at least 3,000/mcL; ANC at least 1,500/mcL; platelets at least 100,000/mcL; total bilirubin under 1.5 x ULN, or for Gilbert syndrome a direct bilirubin under 1.5 x ULN; AST and ALT at or under 2.5 x ULN; creatinine under 1.5 x ULN or measured creatinine clearance over 30 mL/min.

HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible. Known cardiac disease or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class I or II, or objective class A or B. No prior pelvic external-beam RT that would overlap standard fields so that normal-tissue constraints cannot be met. The patient must agree not to father children. English or Spanish is required for the quality-of-life component.

Step 1: Baseline standard PET/CT or PET/MR with an FDA-approved prostate radiotracer must be completed after Step 0 and before randomization, or up to 16 weeks before Step 0, and must establish extra-pelvic disease as positive or negative. No uncontrolled illness, including active infection or tuberculosis, symptomatic CHF, MI or unstable angina, significant uncontrolled arrhythmia, clinically relevant cirrhosis, or interstitial lung disease in the prior 3 months. HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load and CD4 > 250 cells/mcL; chronic HBV allowed if viral load undetectable on suppressive therapy; HCV allowed if treated with undetectable viral load.

Not pregnant and not nursing.

Age 18 or older; ECOG 0-2.

ANC 1,500/mm3 or more, platelets 100,000/mm3 or more, hemoglobin 9 g/dL or more (transfusion allowed); CrCl 30 mL/min or more (Cockcroft-Gault); bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less (3 x ULN or less with Gilbert's); AST and ALT 3 x ULN or less.
Patients with cardiac history, cardiac symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated; HCV must be treated and cured, or undetectable viral load if on treatment.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
No active infection requiring parenteral antibiotics. No intra-abdominal abscess, undiverted abdominal/pelvic fistula, GI perforation or obstruction, or need for nasogastric or gastrostomy drainage.

No malabsorption, chronic diarrhea, or significant GI disease with grade 2 or higher diarrhea or inability to take oral therapy. No lung disease causing dyspnea at rest; no interstitial lung disease with ongoing signs or symptoms.
No allergy to the study agents or chemically similar compounds.
Not pregnant and not nursing.
